backing.backing_score_basis: ⚠️⚠️ NOT AN INHERITANCE FROM usdai 7.0: sUSDai HOLDS A DIFFERENT ASSET SET. usdai's reserve is PYUSD at par; sUSDai holds a USDai idle buffer PLUS a GPU/equipment loan book originated through MetaStreet. Under the spec's 2026-09-11 discriminator a wrapper holding something its underlying does not is scored ON MERITS. ✅ THE OVERCOLLATERALIZATION IS REAL AND STRUCTURED: 70-80% LTV, a ~10% DSRA, sCHIP beneath — a genuine three-layer cushion. ⚠️ BUT THE COLLATERAL DEPRECIATES ON A TECHNOLOGY CURVE RATHER THAN A CREDIT CURVE: GPU and AI hardware, so an LTV struck today is not the LTV at default. Every other loan book in this corpus sits against treasuries, real estate or crypto. ⚠️ AND MOST CAPITAL IS DEPLOYED: loansReserves $104M -> $257.3M, so the idle buffer that absorbed a shock in May is proportionally thinner. ⚠️⚠️ THE DUAL MARK — RE-BASED 2026-09-12, AND THE SCORE DID NOT MOVE BUT ITS REASON DID. This basis previously called the deposit price an OPTIMISTIC MARK and said headline AUM and NAV are 'both optimistic while exits are not'. ⚠️ THAT WORDING IMPLIES THE VAULT IS FLATTERING ITSELF, AND THE DESIGN IS THE OPPOSITE. USD.AI DOCUMENTS IT (docs.usd.ai/depositor/susdai/susdai-withdrawal-estimates, read 2026-09-12): the deposit price 'continuously prorates expected upcoming repayments across all loans in the book' while the redemption price 'is based on settled repayments and realized vault accounting'. ITS STATED PURPOSE IS TO PREVENT YIELD SNIPING — stopping a depositor buying in just before a known repayment to capture a NAV step existing holders earned. It is explicitly offered as an alternative to a fixed redemption fee: 'Some systems use a fixed redemption fee to address this. sUSDai instead uses dynamic forward pricing to make the pricing more economically accurate.' ✅ A DISCLOSED, HOLDER-PROTECTIVE ANTI-ARBITRAGE MECHANISM IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT FROM AN OPTIMISTIC MARK, and the reason is what a reader acts on. ⚠️ WHAT STILL HOLDS THE 5.0: a two-price vault is a real complexity a holder must model, the QEV priority exit is not live on-chain, and a 30-day FIFO queue settling at the conservative price is a genuine exit constraint — none of which the documentation removes.

dependencies.underlying_score_basis: MEASURES THE COUNTERPARTY SET. ⚠️ BELOW usdai's 7.0 (corrected from 5.5 on 2026-09-12), AND THE WRAPPER EQUAL-RULE DOES NOT BIND — sUSDai holds a different asset set, so the spec's discriminator puts it outside the rule. It inherits every counterparty usdai has and adds its own: (1) the whole of usdai's set arrives UNDILUTED — PYUSD, therefore Paxos, therefore PYUSD's reserve banks; (2) METASTREET as originator and servicer of the loan book, a role with NO SUBSTITUTE — if it stops servicing, the loans do not re-home; (3) the BORROWER SET in the GPU/equipment book, whose concentration the Volatility row flags; (4) Permian Labs as operator; (5) four chains — arb, plasma, eth, base. ⚠️⚠️ AND ONE DEPENDENCY THAT RUNS BACKWARDS: sUSDai IS 99.3% OF FLUID'S GHO MARKET ON PLASMA. $8,644,704 posted against $7,411,720 borrowed, 4.26pp of headroom, and a 4.74% mark drop takes that book to its liquidation threshold. That is Fluid depending on sUSDai, not the reverse — BUT THE CHANNEL CLOSES THE LOOP: a liquidation there is forced selling of sUSDai into sUSDai's OWN secondary, moving the mark that triggered it. REFLEXIVITY, NOT COUNTERPARTY EXPOSURE, so it is not priced as reliance — it is recorded because a holder reading only the counterparty list would never see it.
